channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: 47 Students Hospitalized in Almaty with Suspected Intestinal Infection
item.description: Forty-seven students from the Republican Physics and Mathematics School in Almaty were hospitalized with symptoms of acute intestinal infection. The school's activities, dormitory, and canteen have been temporarily suspended pending an investigation and laboratory analysis by sanitary-epidemiological control specialists. The situation is under control.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Fintech Sector: Solva Group Discusses Banking Licenses and Market Strategy
item.description: Galym Khusainov, Chairman of Solva Group Ltd., discusses the trend of microfinance organizations in Kazakhstan transitioning to banks. He emphasizes that a banking license alone is insufficient to compete with established players. Khusainov highlights Solva's focus on building a fintech ecosystem, leveraging AI for financial services, and engaging with regulators and investors.

item.title: Wrestling and Taekwondo Updates: Kazakh Athletes Reach Finals, Win Medals
item.description: Kazakh wrestlers Aybek Aitbekov and Yusuf Ashrapov have advanced to the finals of the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas. In taekwondo, Maria Sevostyanova secured a bronze medal at the Paris Grand Prix. The Barys ice hockey club lost their recent Kontinental Hockey League match. The U19 World Boxing Championships are set to begin in Budva, Montenegro.

item.title: Xi Jinping Calls for Progress in 'Healthy China' Initiative During 15th Five-Year Plan Period
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged efforts to advance the 'Healthy China' program during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Speaking at a national health conference, he emphasized that national health is crucial for prosperity and strength. Xi highlighted historical successes since 2012 in building a comprehensive medical service system and stressed prevention as the most effective healthcare approach.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes One-Time Aid of 1 Million Som for Over a Million Needy Families
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed a one-time financial aid of 1 million som for over one million needy families starting November. This initiative aims to support households lacking gas supply during the heating season by expanding electricity, gas, and coal compensation. The plan is part of a presidential decree aimed at social protection, with an estimated 1.9 trillion som allocated by 2026.

item.title: Two Ships Attacked in Strait of Hormuz, Maritime Trade Center Reports
item.description: The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that two ships, a tanker and a container ship, were attacked with projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The origin of the projectiles is currently unknown. This follows reports of at least 12 commercial ships being targeted in the region over the past week, marking the highest weekly total since the start of recent conflicts.

item.title: Karaganda Region Akim Expresses Shame Over Unpaid Wages for Agricultural Station Workers
item.description: Workers at the Karaganda Agricultural Experimental Station have not received wages since June, accumulating debts and struggling with utility payments. The regional akim acknowledged the difficult situation, stating it's 'uncomfortable to look them in the eye.' The enterprise's chairman promised to gradually settle the salary arrears.

item.title: New Fully Automated Rice Processing Plant Launched in Kyzylorda
item.description: A new, fully automated rice processing plant has been launched in Kyzylorda by 'Abzal & K' LLP. This project is a significant step in developing the region's processing industry. The plant utilizes modern rice processing lines and GPS monitoring, operating on solar power, and processes 98% of the delivered rice.

item.title: New Social Facilities Opened in Arkalyk to Support Children with Disabilities
item.description: Two new social facilities have been launched in Arkalyk with the support of the 'Kazakhstan Khalkyna' public fund. One is a pediatric medical rehabilitation center opened at the regional hospital. It will provide services to children with neurological conditions from Arkalyk and surrounding districts, as well as from the Akmola region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Restore 4 Million Hectares of Pastureland by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to restore 4 million hectares of degraded pastureland by 2027. Currently, only 40% of the country's over 21 million hectares of pastureland is effectively utilized. A plan is in place to reduce degraded areas by 20% next year.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Government Bonds See Increased Non-Resident Investment Amidst Currency Market Risks
item.description: Non-resident investment in Kazakhstan's government bonds surged by 2.3 times in dollar terms over the past year, reaching $5.6 billion. This growth, driven by a high base interest rate and a strengthening tenge, suggests activity from carry traders. Analysts warn of potential currency market instability if this trend continues.

item.title: Almaty School Suspends Operations Following Mass Food Poisoning Outbreak Among Students
item.description: The Republican Physics and Mathematics School (RFMS) in Almaty has suspended its operations after 47 students were hospitalized with acute intestinal infections. Health authorities have temporarily closed the school and its dining facilities pending an investigation into the source of the outbreak. Medical teams are monitoring the affected students.

item.title: 14-Year-Old Girl Dies in Hospital; Parents Blame Doctors
item.description: A 14-year-old girl, Kamshat Serash, has died in a children's hospital in Kyzylorda. Her parents allege that doctors misdiagnosed her condition, failing to detect a brain hemorrhage in time. They claim she was treated for a stomach ailment after experiencing severe headaches and vomiting. The family seeks justice for their daughter's death.

item.title: New War Risk: Ethiopia Deploys Troops to Eritrean Border Amid Accusations
item.description: Ethiopia has deployed troops to its border with Eritrea, citing a new war risk. Both neighboring countries have appealed to the UN, accusing each other of military aggression. The situation remains tense as diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the conflict are underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets Snap Maslikhat Elections for November 29
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has scheduled snap elections for maslikhat deputies at all levels for November 29. The decision was made on October 13. A total of 3,447 deputies will be elected across 228 maslikhats. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev had previously signed a decree dissolving all maslikhats, citing changes in the party system.

item.title: Akmola Region Expands Cooperation with Belgian and Australian Companies
item.description: The Akmola region in Kazakhstan is enhancing its economic ties with Belgian and Australian firms. Agreements include expanding grain and oilseed exports to Europe via Baltic ports and Belgium. Australian investors are considering a $150 million rare earth metal processing plant. Steppe­nogorsk may become a global magnet production center.

item.title: Aktobe Faces Funding Shortfall for New Water Pipeline, Leaving Thousands Without Supply
item.description: Over a thousand homes in the Rauan-2 district of Aktobe remain without centralized water supply as the new pipeline project is 90% complete but lacks 796 million tenge for finalization. Residents have been independently transporting water for over a decade and fear road conditions will worsen with rain. The project, funded by the regional budget, requires additional funds for completion.

item.title: Samarkand to Host International Astronautical Congress in 2028
item.description: Samarkand, Uzbekistan, has been selected to host the International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in 2028. This major event will bring together space agency representatives, scientists, and experts to discuss the future of space technology and international cooperation. Previous congresses were held in Antalya (2026) and Poznan (2027), with Geneva scheduled for 2029.

item.title: UN Reports 1.2 Billion People Living in Multidimensional Poverty
item.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) reports that approximately 1.2 billion people worldwide are living in multidimensional poverty, an increase of 51.5 million. The global multidimensional poverty index, established in 2010, shows this is the first time the figure has risen. Around 83% of those in poverty reside in rural areas, with children making up over half the total.

item.title: Almaty Homebuyers Demand Action on Unfinished Housing Projects
item.description: Hundreds of families in Almaty are demanding the city administration's help with unfinished housing projects. Buyers have paid for apartments in seven residential complexes but have not received them, with some homes ordered for demolition due to construction violations. Many fear losing their investments and homes.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews New Pasture Restoration and Usage Procedures
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed a presentation on preventing pasture degradation, improving water supply, and ensuring effective land use. Uzbekistan has 21.2 million hectares of pastures, but only 40% are effectively utilized. The president stressed the importance of utilizing this potential for food security. Tasks were set to restore 620,000 hectares this year and 3.7 million next year.

item.title: Kazakh Journalist's Widow Details Transnational Repression and Husband's Murder Investigation
item.description: Natalia Sadykova, widow of slain Kazakh journalist Aidos Sadykov, spoke at an OSCE event about ongoing persecution after her husband's murder. She detailed diplomatic espionage, alleged judicial sabotage by Kazakh oligarchs in Ukraine, and digital censorship targeting independent media BACE. Sadykova criticized Kazakhstan's official investigation into her husband's killing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sells State's 49.07% Stake in UzXCMG Joint Venture for Mining Equipment
item.description: Uzbekistan is selling the state's 49.07% share in the UzXCMG joint venture, located in Urgench, Khorezm region. The company specializes in manufacturing equipment for mining and underground work. The starting price is set at 140.53 billion UZS, with an auction scheduled for October 19.

item.title: Turkmenistan Expands Multilateral Cooperation for Global Prosperity
item.description: Independent and perpetually neutral Turkmenistan continues to successfully implement its broad cooperation strategy, initiated by National Leader Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov and led by President Serdar Berdimuhamedov. The country is enhancing its reputation as a reliable partner regionally and globally. Recent events included significant foreign and domestic policy developments, focusing on socio-economic and spiritual progress.

item.title: Russia Destroys 18 Tons of Contaminated Tomatoes from Turkmenistan
item.description: Russian authorities in the Omsk region destroyed 18 tons of tomatoes imported from Turkmenistan due to the detection of the Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus. The contaminated shipment was identified at a temporary storage warehouse and subsequently incinerated to prevent the disease's spread into the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan President to Attend CICA Summit in Baku
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Azerbaijan on October 14-15 to participate in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The summit in Baku will focus on strengthening trust, peace, and security in Asia, and institutional development of CICA.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 5.5 Million Hectares of Pastureland to Rural Residents
item.description: Kazakhstan has provided 5.5 million hectares of pastureland to rural residents, significantly reducing pastureland shortages. This initiative, part of a presidential directive, aims to support livestock farming and rural development. The Ministry of Agriculture reported that 13 million hectares have been returned to state control, with 5.5 million designated for public grazing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Annual Heating Tariff Increases Up to 10% from 2028
item.description: Uzbekistan is proposing to increase centralized heating tariffs annually by up to 10%, starting from 2028, adjusted for inflation. The Ministry of Construction and Housing and Communal Services drafted the proposal. Tariffs will be indexed annually from May 1st, with increases not exceeding 10%. The plan also includes separate tariff hikes for heating and hot water from November 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Halving Land and Property Taxes for Household Greenhouses
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering a proposal to halve land and property taxes for household greenhouses. Owners of these greenhouses would also be exempt from turnover tax. Additionally, half the cost of electricity for energy-efficient systems would be covered.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Special Ecological Regime for Greenhouses in Tashkent Region
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed a special ecological regime for greenhouses in Tashkent and surrounding areas, focusing on 'green' technologies. Allowed heating sources include natural gas, electricity, geothermal, and solar energy. Burning tires, plastic, bitumen, or waste is prohibited. Greenhouses using solid fuel must switch to approved sources by December 1st, with exceptions for those meeting strict technical requirements.

item.title: Customs Regime Boosts Export Potential Through Tax Exemptions
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing measures to expand production and support exports. The 'Processing within the customs territory' regime offers exemptions from VAT, excise tax, and customs duties, aiding businesses. Navoiy region imported over $22.9 million in raw materials for processing in early 2026. Solis Olis LLC utilizes these benefits to produce vegetable oil for domestic and international markets.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Special Tax Regimes for Self-Employed, Businesses, and Farmers
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced special tax regimes to optimize taxation for various business types. Self-employed individuals will pay 4% for social purposes. Businesses on a simplified declaration basis will have a 4% rate, adjustable by local authorities. Farmers and peasant farms will pay a 0.5% individual income tax. These measures aim to create favorable conditions for entrepreneurship.

item.title: Zelensky: Air Raid Sirens Silent During Russian Attack on Kyiv; West Did Not Warn
item.description: Air raid sirens did not sound during Russia's ballistic missile attack on Kyiv on October 12. Sirens activated only after initial explosions. Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that Western partners provided no prior intelligence regarding the impending attack. Russia launched five ballistic missiles at the capital.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry Assesses Impact of Russian Gas Pipeline Explosion
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has commented on an explosion at the Central Asia-Center gas pipeline in Russia's Penza region. The ministry stated that gas supply to Kazakhstan continues normally under existing contracts. Transit of gas to Uzbekistan through Kazakhstan is also proceeding as planned. No deviations in Kazakhstan's gas transportation system have been recorded.

item.title: Taliban Ministry Orders Review of All Residential Township Documentation
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban Ministry of Urban Development and Housing has mandated that owners of all residential townships nationwide submit their documents, records, and plans for review. This measure aims to ensure urban order, enforce planning regulations, and prevent violations. Owners in Kabul and provinces have one month to comply with the directive.

item.title: Kazakh Hospitals and Polyclinics Received 1.9 Trillion Tenge via Social Health Insurance Fund
item.description: Kazakhstan's hospitals and polyclinics received 1.933 trillion tenge over nine months in 2026 through the Social Health Insurance Fund (FMSM). Finance Minister Madi Takiev reported that funds were transferred from the state budget to FMSM, which then allocated them to medical organizations. An information system, Qalqan, now integrates FMSM and treasury payment processes.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government to Fund Upcoming Maslikhat Elections from Reserve Funds
item.description: Funds for the upcoming maslikhat (local assembly) elections in Kazakhstan will be allocated from the government's reserve funds, as they were not included in the current budget. The Central Election Commission stated that the total cost depends on the number of commissions, campaign duration, and organizational factors. Approximately 75-80% of expenses will cover commission member payments.

item.title: Taliban Fighters Allegedly Steal Valuables from Kabul Home Posing as Justice Ministry Delegation
item.description: Local sources report that armed Taliban fighters, identifying themselves as an inspection delegation from the Ministry of Justice, robbed a house in Kabul's Omid-e Sabz Township. Five fighters allegedly confined residents and stole valuables. Residents complain of increasing lawlessness and mistreatment by the Taliban, with some families reportedly forced to vacate their homes.

item.title: UN Launches Disaster Protection Projects in Baghlan Province Following Devastating Floods
item.description: The UN Development Programme (UNDP) in Afghanistan is implementing flood protection infrastructure in Baghlan Province through the PAIDAAR project. Supported by the Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan, the initiative aims to reduce flood risks and protect homes, agricultural land, and livelihoods, emphasizing community resilience and disaster preparedness.

item.title: IOM Reports 112 Disaster Risk Reduction Projects Implemented Across Afghanistan Since 2025
item.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has implemented 112 projects across Afghanistan to reduce natural disaster risks since 2025. The organization emphasized that preparedness and early action strengthen resilience in vulnerable areas, while also enhancing local capacities in coordination and technical skills for disaster risk reduction.
